results.summary_before: This design implements a six-digit seven-segment clock displaying hours, minutes and seconds. Two active-high pushbuttons increment hours and minutes for setting the time, and the decimal points blink once per second. It requires a 32768 Hz clock, a six-digit common-anode display, and six PMOS/PNP digit-enable transistors. The outputs include active-low segment drives and multiplexed digit enables, and the design is intended for breadboard or custom PCB assembly.

results.summary_before: KianV uLinux RISC-V regfile edition is a 32-bit RISC-V IMA processor capable of booting Linux, featuring a 32x32 register file macro. It includes external SPI flash and PSRAM interfaces, a UART, and a SPI peripheral. The system runs at 30 MHz and requires a QSPI Pmod for external memory. Silicon tests showed partial functionality: it could not boot Linux due to an impedance mismatch when integrating the register file, though the register file itself works.
